question: We have two tests to diagnose a serious prognosis disease. Test A has a sensitivity of 95% and a specificity of 60% and test B has a sensitivity of 70% and a specificity of 99%. We have an effective treatment but that produces important adverse effects and also has a very high cost. What test would we choose to make the diagnosis?

options.opa: Test A because it will detect less false positives.
options.opb: Test A because it has a higher sensitivity.
options.opc: Test B because it will detect more false positives.
options.opd: Test A because it will detect more false negatives.
options.ope: Test B because it has a greater specificity.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Test A has a sensitivity of -> 95%
CHAIN: Test B has a sensitivity of -> 70%

CHAIN: Test A has a higher sensitivity than Test B -> Higher sensitivity means fewer false negatives with Test A -> Test A's specificity is lower than Test B's -> Lower specificity means more false positives with Test A -> In a serious prognosis disease, detecting all cases is more critical than avoiding false positives -> Confidence in choosing Test A is -> 90%

CHAIN: Test B has a greater specificity than Test A -> Greater specificity means fewer false positives with Test B -> Test B's sensitivity is lower than Test A's -> Lower sensitivity means more false negatives with Test B -> In a serious prognosis disease, missing a diagnosis can be detrimental -> Confidence in choosing Test B is -> 70%
analysis: In this scenario, we have to consider the implications of sensitivity and specificity in relation to the disease's serious prognosis and the treatment's adverse effects and high cost. Test A has a higher sensitivity (95%), meaning it is more likely to correctly identify those with the disease, which is crucial given the serious nature of the disease. However, it has a lower specificity (60%), leading to more false positives. Test B, while having a lower sensitivity (70%), has a much higher specificity (99%), meaning it is more reliable in confirming the absence of the disease. Given the high cost and adverse effects of the treatment, it is important to minimize unnecessary treatment. Therefore, Test B, with its greater specificity, would be the better choice to avoid false positives and unnecessary treatment, despite its lower sensitivity. Thus, the best option is to choose Test B for diagnosis.
